newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - French shares lower but steady.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - French shares lower but steady.

text.p: French companies' American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were steady at lower levels Monday amid jitters about the victory of the Socialist Party and its leftist allies in French parliamentary elections.
Traders said French shares were being supported as U.S. investors adopted a wait-and-see attitude toward the Socialist win in the Sunday vote.
"The French shares really got pounded early ... and I think it was a lot of late buying by American houses" that buoyed the ADRs, one trader said.

Among French shares, engineering company Alcatel Alsthom fell 1-1/4 to 21-1/2. The firm has been a bidder for electronics company Thomson-CSF, due to be privatized by the former conservative government.
The planned privatization has been thrown into doubt by the election results.
Oil companies fell. Elf Aquitaine was down 1/2 to 51-5/8 and Total SA was off 1/2 to 45-1/8.
Luxury goods company LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton rose 1/2 to 49-1/8.
Among other European shares, Swedish phone equipment maker Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson was up 1/8 to 35-3/4.
Clothing company Tommy Hilfiger Corp, based in the British Virgin Islands, fell 1-1/2 to 43 after it reported fourth-quarter earnings per share of $0.59, up from $0.48 a year earlier.
Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd rose 1/8 to 22-3/4 in heavy volume.
Advancers led decliners 237 to 211 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group rose 0.03 percent and volume in late morning was 25.5 million shares.
ADRs allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
